contents.text: How does the 2027 parental leave policy differ from the 2024 one?

The 2027 parental leave policy increases the paid leave from 16 to 20 weeks. The 2027 policy allows taking the leave in up to three blocks, whereas the 2024 policy requires one continuous block within 12 months. The 2027 policy does not change the six-month service requirement or the full pay for the leave.

Parental leave policy (2024)
# Parental leave policy (2024)
Employees with at least six months of service receive 16 weeks of paid parental leave after the birth or adoption of a child.
The leave must be taken in one continuous block within 12 months of the birth or adoption, at 100 percent of base salary.
Employees agree the start date with their manager at least eight weeks in advance.
Employees on parental leave keep their pension contributions and accrue annual leave as if they were working.

HR guidance: parental leave changes for 2027
# HR guidance: parental leave changes for 2027
This guidance is restricted to HR and people managers until the change is announced on February 15, 2027.
From March 1, 2027, paid parental leave increases from 16 to 20 weeks and can be taken in up to three blocks.
The six-month service requirement and full pay are unchanged.
Employees whose leave starts before March 1, 2027 stay on the 2024 policy.
Managers should send questions to their HR business partner.
## Questions managers may hear
Employees may ask whether they can split leave they have already started.
They can't: the three-block rule applies only to leave that starts on or after March 1, 2027.
Employees on fixed-term contracts receive the same leave if their contract runs for at least six months beyond the start of the leave.
